scenarios.title: Server storage holds no plaintext
scenarios.expected: No readable content; ciphertext looks random
scenarios.observed: marker present in stored file: False; entropy 7.999 bits/byte (plaintext 4.56)

scenarios.title: Same file sent twice gives unrelated ciphertext
scenarios.expected: Fresh key and IV per transfer
scenarios.observed: 0.38% of ciphertext bytes coincide (chance level is 0.39%)

scenarios.title: A different private key cannot recover the file key
scenarios.observed: client check: 'this private key is not the key the sender encrypted for'; raw OAEP unwrap: 'cannot unwrap key: this transfer was not encrypted for your key'

scenarios.title: One bit flipped in the ciphertext (hash check)
scenarios.observed: ciphertext hash does not match server metadata

scenarios.title: One bit flipped, hash check bypassed (MAC check)
scenarios.observed: MAC verification failed: ciphertext was modified or key is wrong

scenarios.title: IV modified
scenarios.observed: MAC verification failed: ciphertext was modified or key is wrong

scenarios.title: MAC tag modified
scenarios.observed: MAC verification failed: ciphertext was modified or key is wrong

scenarios.title: Ciphertext truncated by three blocks
scenarios.expected: Rejected as malformed or by the MAC
scenarios.observed: MAC verification failed: ciphertext was modified or key is wrong

scenarios.title: Ciphertext swapped for another valid ciphertext
scenarios.expected: Hash mismatch; MAC fails under the right key
scenarios.observed: hash check: 'ciphertext hash does not match server metadata'; MAC under original key: 'MAC verification failed: ciphertext was modified or key is wrong'

scenarios.title: Stored file altered on the server's disk
scenarios.expected: Server refuses to serve it and audits the event
scenarios.observed: HTTP 500 'stored evidence failed integrity check'; audit entry STORAGE_TAMPER_DETECTED recorded: True

scenarios.title: Signature forged with another officer's key
Any signed field changed after signing
scenarios.expected: Every variant rejected (filename, type, size, recipient)

scenarios.title: Registering a key without proof of possession
Retired key can no longer sign uploads
Other investigator requests Bob's evidence
Sender requests the ciphertext back
Another officer requests Bob's evidence
Administrator requests Bob's evidence
Unknown and forbidden IDs are indistinguishable
scenarios.expected: Same answer, so IDs cannot be probed

scenarios.title: Investigator tries to upload evidence
Non-admins read the audit log
Inbox shows only your own evidence
Request without a token
Invented token
Expired token
Token used after logout
Password guessing
scenarios.expected: Account locks after 5 failures, even for the right password
scenarios.observed: 5 wrong guesses→[401, 401, 401, 401, 401]; correct password afterwards→HTTP 429 (account temporarily locked)

scenarios.title: Passwords and tokens are stored hashed
scenarios.expected: No plaintext secrets in the database
scenarios.observed: password stored as 'pbkdf2:sha256:1000$PeW…', session token stored as SHA-256 '0edeeab1aeca1d0d…'

scenarios.title: Exact copy of an upload resent
Upload signed an hour ago
Upload signed an hour in the future
SQL injection and path traversal in the transfer ID
SQL injection in the login form
Upload larger than the limit
scenarios.observed: HTTP 413 (limit set to 2 MB for this run)

scenarios.title: Upload that is not an EVC1 envelope
scenarios.observed: HTTP 400: ciphertext is not a valid EVC1 envelope

scenarios.title: Connection dropped mid-upload
Server unreachable
scenarios.expected: Client fails fast with a clear error

scenarios.title: Chain of custody verifies after all the activity above
A log entry is edited in the database
scenarios.observed: edited entry #1; verifier reports ok=False, first bad entry #1

scenarios.title: A log entry is deleted from the database
Chain verifies again once the rows are restored
scenarios.expected: Chain intact (proves the checks above were real)
